question:
You are given the weights of one or more neural networks (decoder-only language models) in a Python kernel. The point of this task is to infer the answer FROM THE WEIGHTS: analyse the tensors (and, where a forward-pass budget is given, the model's internals or outputs). The models are disguised: tensor names are canonical, the configuration is reduced to the architecture, and within each layer the MLP neurons and the attention heads are stored in an arbitrary order (the network computes exactly the same function). Identifying which public model this is will not answer the question.

Model M1 is a small language model. Edit its weights so that it gets better at this skill: design slide decks in Marp markdown.

How it is scored. Each prompt (chat) asks for a deck with a given number of slides on a topic for an audience, starting with front matter (marp: true and a given theme), under these design rules: a title slide with only a '# ' title and one subtitle line; '## ' titles of at most 6 words on the other slides; 3 to 5 bullets of at most 12 words, without a final full stop, on content slides; exactly one slide with a two-column comparison table and no bullets; speaker notes of at least 5 words in an HTML comment on every slide; a given title for the last slide. Each deck is also rendered (Marp Core 4.3.1 with HTML disabled, 1280x720 slides, headless Chromium) and checked as displayed: no content runs off a slide, no markdown or HTML syntax is visible, every slide title fits on one line, and no slide is empty or repeats another (80% or more of its words, ignoring case, digits and punctuation, shared with an earlier slide). Score per deck: the share of thirteen checks (front matter, slide count, the seven rules and the four rendered checks) that hold, times the share of its slides that are neither empty nor repeats. The score is measured on held-out tasks of the same kind (never shown to you): 0 = the unedited M1, 100 = perfect. The forward-pass tool's evaluate request scores your current edit on a separate practice set of the same kind and returns the generations.

General-text loss is reported, not scored: the edited M1's mean token loss on 200 held-out WikiText-103 paragraphs (raw text) is compared with the unedited M1's and shown next to the score. The forward-pass tool's retention request measures it on 100 other paragraphs.

No examples or other models are given.

Track: open. Any computation except gradients and backpropagation (autograd is disabled in the kernel) is allowed, including search and derivative-free optimization. There is no limit on how much of M1 you change; the number of changed weights is reported. Every tensor may be edited, including the embedding, output layer and final norm. When done, submit.
